summary: The biblical common noun occurs in the plural. Its construct form introduces descriptions of a group, while a numeral or expression of number can specify how few people it contains.

senses.definition: Psalm 17 twice asks for deliverance from men, describing the portion they receive in this life. Elsewhere men are distinguished by the company they keep or by their conduct.
Jacob says his people are few in number, and the same expression describes the small household that went down to Egypt.

evidence.locator: mutu [husband] N, armep x000002960; forms include mutum and mutiša

note: The Akkadian noun has the narrower sense husband. Methuselah already has a name entry under the second part of that name. The first element of Methushael may also preserve the old word for man.
